review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked for repeated reasoning blocks: evalAt_add/evalAt_mul/evalAt_sub_algebraMap, the adicValuation-to-exp conversions, evalAt_algebraMap/residue_algebraMap, and the ord = 1 lemmas. Most repetitions are short, routine rewrite patterns, so I did not report them. The only duplication I judged worth reporting is the three-step derivation (nonzero, then membership of the difference, then membership of t) copied between evalAt_eq_of_ord_sub_algebraMap_eq_one and mem_of_ord_sub_algebraMap_eq_one. The `ord t = 1 → t ≠ 0` argument is also inlined twice and is already packaged as ne_zero_of_ord_eq_one, which is declared after both. I did not run Lean, so the rewrite below is untested. The cleanup is modest in size.

findings.excerpt:
have hne : t - algebraMap K F c ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0; rw [h0, Place.ord_zero] at h; exact zero_ne_one h
  have hmem : t - algebraMap K F c ∈ w.toValuationSubring := mem_of_ord_nonneg w hne (by omega)
findings.problem: The first two theorems each re-prove the same facts from `w.ord (t - algebraMap K F c) = 1`. They prove `t - algebraMap K F c ≠ 0`, then membership of the difference in the valuation subring, then membership of `t` via `add_mem` and `simpa`. The nonzero argument is also repeated verbatim in `ne_zero_of_ord_eq_one`, which is declared after both and so is not reused. evalAt_eq_of_ord_sub_algebraMap_eq_one repeats the whole of mem_of_ord_sub_algebraMap_eq_one as its `ht` step.
findings.proposed_change: Reorder the declarations. Put `ne_zero_of_ord_eq_one` first, then `mem_of_ord_sub_algebraMap_eq_one`, then `evalAt_eq_of_ord_sub_algebraMap_eq_one`. Proof of the membership lemma: `have hne := ne_zero_of_ord_eq_one w h; have hmem : t - algebraMap K F c ∈ w.toValuationSubring := mem_of_ord_nonneg w hne (by omega); simpa using add_mem hmem (w.algebraMap_mem' c)`. Proof of the evalAt lemma: `have hne := ne_zero_of_ord_eq_one w h; have ht := mem_of_ord_sub_algebraMap_eq_one w t c h; have h0 : w.evalAt (t - algebraMap K F c) = 0 := evalAt_eq_zero_of_ord_pos w hne (by omega); rw [evalAt_sub_algebraMap w hw ht c] at h0; exact sub_eq_zero.mp h0`. This drops the local `hmem`, which the evalAt lemma never needs beyond producing `ht`. Both lemmas keep their current hypotheses (`hw` is still required only for evalAt), and no new imports are needed.
findings.benefit: The "ord of t − c is 1 implies t is integral and nonzero" reasoning then lives in one place, so a change to it needs one edit. The evalAt lemma reads as its real content (the difference vanishes at the place, hence `evalAt t = c`). `ne_zero_of_ord_eq_one` is also used later by `Setup.sub_ne_zero`, so it is already the intended API.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem ne_zero_of_ord_eq_one (w : Place K F) {t : F} (h : w.ord t = 1) : t ≠ 0 := by
  intro h0; rw [h0, Place.ord_zero] at h; exact zero_ne_one h

have hmem : t - algebraMap K F c ∈ w.toValuationSubring := mem_of_ord_nonneg w hne (by omega)
  simpa using add_mem hmem (w.algebraMap_mem' c)
